name: Work as One Whole: Time, Rate, and Remaining Work
description: Turn completion time into a daily work rate and use it to track completed and remaining work.
script_scope: Teach the chapter's core model: take the whole job as 1. If A finishes in n days, A's one-day work is 1/n; if a worker completes only a stated fraction in some days, first recover the whole-job time or daily rate. Cover work completed in several days, remaining work, two and three workers combining, and jobs larger than one unit such as producing two identical items. Emphasize rate × time = work and work ÷ rate = time.

name: Combined Workers and Hidden Individual Rates
description: Recover an unknown worker or helper rate from together-times and known individual rates.
script_scope: Teach subtraction of work rates: if A+B have a known rate and B is known, then A is the difference. Extend to a third helper, one known pair plus an individual, partial-work clues that reveal an individual's whole-job time, and questions where a worker completes the remainder after another has worked first. Keep the unknown as a rate before converting it back into days.

name: Efficiency, Relative Speed, and Working Hours
description: Convert statements about efficiency, speed, and daily hours into comparable work rates and times.
script_scope: Teach that efficiency is proportional to work rate and inversely proportional to completion time. Cover twice/thrice as efficient, percentage more or less efficient, fixed differences in completion times, same worker working different hours per day, and workers with different hourly rates and daily schedules. Include the chapter pattern where a job time in days of h hours must first be converted into total working hours.

name: Pairwise Teams and Reverse Work Relations
description: Use AB, BC, and AC team rates or algebraic relationships to recover individual workers.
script_scope: Teach pairwise-rate identities. From AB, BC and AC rates, add them to get twice the ABC rate, then subtract a pair to recover an individual. Cover finding the fastest worker, an individual when A equals the combined rate of B and C, and reverse relations such as B taking a multiple of the time taken by A+C. Include simple reciprocal equations where a together-time and a difference or ratio between individual times determine the workers.

name: Joining, Leaving, and Replacement Timelines
description: Split a job into stages when workers join late, leave early, or replace one another.
script_scope: Teach piecewise work timelines. Cover one worker starting alone before another joins, all workers starting together before someone leaves, a worker leaving a fixed number of days before completion, one worker being replaced by another, and several workers leaving at different stages. At every stage identify active workers, stage duration, work completed, and remaining work before moving on.

name: Changing Workforce and Deadline Problems
description: Use worker-days to handle people joining, leaving, absenteeism, and deadline adjustments.
script_scope: Teach equal-efficiency workforce questions using worker-days. Cover workers joining after part of a job is done, workers leaving and causing delay, finding the original workforce from a delayed finish, hiring extra workers to meet a deadline, and calculating how far behind schedule a team would be without reinforcement. Distinguish these from mixed-efficiency problems: worker-days works directly only when workers are equivalent.

name: Alternating Days and Periodic Assistance
description: Solve repeating work schedules by finding the work done in one full cycle and then the leftover.
script_scope: Teach alternating and periodic schedules. Cover A and B working on alternate days, a main worker assisted every second or third day, three workers taking turns, and cases where a worker is present every day while helpers alternate. Find work per cycle, count complete cycles, then handle the final fraction in the correct turn order; include fractional final days and wage shares based on actual work done.

name: Wages, Earnings, and Work Shares
description: Divide payment according to actual work done, including different daily wages or working durations.
script_scope: Teach that payment for a completed job is divided in the ratio of work contributions, not simply time spent. Cover two-worker wage splits from completion times, a helper added to finish early, daily wage ratios combined with different days worked, recovering daily wages from total earnings, a fixed fund paying workers for different numbers of days, and efficiency-linked wage comparisons. Include the chapter pattern of A+B and B+C work fractions to recover A's share.

name: Men, Women, Boys, and Equivalent Worker Groups
description: Convert different worker types to a common efficiency unit and solve mixed-group work problems.
script_scope: Teach equivalence between worker categories. Derive one man's, woman's, or boy's rate from group completion data, convert mixed teams into a common worker unit, and combine them. Cover direct equivalences such as 3 men = 6 boys, independent completion-time data for groups, simultaneous equations from two mixed-team conditions, workers joining/leaving in mixed groups, and finding how many of one worker type are required.

name: Machines, Typists, and Output-Rate Work Problems
description: Apply the same work-rate model to pages, machines, conveyors, spindles, and production output.
script_scope: Transfer time-and-work reasoning to output rates. Cover pages per hour, machines producing a fixed batch, conveyor throughput, combined production, a hidden machine rate from a target together-time, splitting work between typists so they finish together, and symbolic production rates such as p machines each making q units in r minutes. Keep units explicit and add rates only after converting them to the same output-per-time unit.

name: Data Sufficiency for Time and Work
description: Judge whether statements give enough independent rate information to answer a time-and-work question.
script_scope: Teach the chapter's data-sufficiency patterns. Cover both statements needed, either statement alone sufficient, even both insufficient, equivalent or redundant statements, pairwise team rates, efficiency ratios, mixed worker groups, required workforce, and three-statement necessity/redundancy questions. The learner should identify the exact rate or relation required before calculating and stop as soon as uniqueness is proved.
